record.body:
This Signature design specifies a field recorder for biofonics work, as a design document rather than a product. The design states a sampling rate of 48000 hertz for audible work and 192000 hertz for ultrasonic work, a microphone sensitivity figure, a calibration procedure using a reference tone, and a metadata schema covering location, time, weather, habitat, equipment, and layer notes. It specifies long, unbroken takes, honest file labelling, and a rule that the recordist stays silent and out of the recording. The design covers all three layers, because a field recorder captures them together and the metadata must note each layer's presence. No hardware is sold or claimed to exist: this is a design specification that a builder could follow, labelled Signature throughout.

Science proof

Science proof: the design follows published bioacoustics practice: sampling rate determines the Nyquist limit, calibration enables loudness comparison, and metadata enables archival reuse. Stating those requirements as a design specification, with numbers, is how real recorder designs are documented, and the Signature design can be checked requirement by requirement against published practice.

Math proof

Math proof: the Nyquist limit is half the sampling rate, so 48000 / 2 = 24000 hertz for audible work and 192000 / 2 = 96000 hertz for ultrasonic work. The demo prints 24000 Hz and 96000 Hz, plus the recording duration for 48000 samples per second over 3600 seconds, 48000 x 3600 = 172,800,000 samples.

Soundscape layer(s)

biophony; geophony; anthrophony

Source

Signature design study for this database, October 2026; bioacoustics methods as in the public edition
